thread:
Noah: quick sync — need 3 crisp competitive claims for next week's launch assets: blog + webinar + battlecard. Audience: infra/platform buyers and SEs. keep each claim one line.

Sofia: propose: 1) predictable unit economics for production workloads; 2) resilient tail latency with automated fallbacks; 3) one runtime, many deployment choices.

Ben: love it. sales needs two rebut lines per claim. quick drafts: 
- Predictable econ rebut: 'We remove per-request variability so finance can forecast spend, without sacrificing throughput.' 
- Tail latency rebut: 'Automatic fallback to quantized or regional variants keeps the app responsive under spikes.'
- Runtime rebut: 'Same API across hosted/dedicated/private — no rewrite when you scale.'

Tara: benchmark guidance: show p50/p95/p99 and cost per 1M tokens. include tiny methodology: '5k anonymized prompts, median 100 tokens.' avoid absolute words.

Noah: legal note — avoid "cheapest" or "always". use comparative language like "lower unit cost in typical production patterns."

Sofia: promo headline A/B ideas: 
A: 'Predictable price. Predictable performance.' 
B: 'One API from prototype to SLA.'

Ben: sales snippets for battlecard: one-liners + objection counters. add customer quote slot for econ story.

Tara: ops wants a single failure-modes slide: flow = quantized fallback -> region reroute -> queued bursts. will make simple diagram.

ops-bot: created doc: https://notion.redwood/competitive/lighthouse-claims (v1) :white_check_mark:

Noah: action list: Noah — write 2 headline variants + 60s webinar opener (today); Sofia — finalize claim wording + rebut bullets (EOD); Ben — collect SE rebut examples + customer quote (48h); Tara — draft chart + failure-modes slide (tomorrow).

Sofia: dropping a 1-line beta quote: 'Switching to Dedicated made our monthly inference spend predictable.'

Noah: perfect. keep it tight and testable. we'll iterate after Ben's SE feedback. :rocket:
